page_title: Transmission Remote GUI — native macOS remote

summary.name: Transmission Remote GUI
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source (MIT) native macOS SwiftUI app that remotely controls a Transmission BitTorrent daemon running on a NAS, seedbox, Raspberry Pi or home server.
keywords: download torrents on server from mac
use_cases: Control a Transmission daemon on a NAS or seedbox from a Mac
Watch media while it is still downloading via sequential streaming
Automatically seed or stop torrents per tracker with ratio and idle rules
Auto-add torrents from RSS feeds with text or regex rules
Monitor torrent speeds from the macOS menu bar
Connect to a server behind a reverse proxy that requires client certificates
summary.what_it_does: The app connects over Transmission's RPC API to a daemon running elsewhere, so downloading and seeding happen on the server while the Mac acts as a remote control. It lists torrents with sortable and customizable columns, sidebar filters by status, tracker, folder and label, and a details panel with files, peers and trackers. Per-tracker, label or name rules set seed ratio, idle limits, speed limits or labels, with a dry run before changes apply. It also provides sequential streaming (Transmission 4.1+), RSS auto-download, live speed graphs, a bandwidth scheduler and turtle mode.
notable: Sequential streaming download of media while it downloads (Transmission 4.1+)
Per-tracker torrent rules with dry run; ratio and idle limits enforced by the daemon even when the app is closed
Menu-bar popover, Keychain password storage, and optional mTLS client certificates
Multilingual UI in English, Hungarian and Simplified Chinese
caveats: Requires a running Transmission daemon with RPC enabled; it does not download torrents by itself
Sequential streaming needs a Transmission 4.1+ daemon
The .dmg is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so first launch requires right-click → Open
